Noah (People Ops): Quick question thread for managers rolling promos mid-June. two managers already pinged me, so saving answers here.
Eli (Eng Manager): If a promo is backdated and payroll does retro, do we show the raise date as the effective date or payroll process date in Workday?
Sam (Payroll): Effective date should be the promo effective date (e.g., 2025-06-01). payroll will process retro adjustments separately but the employee record keeps the effective date.
Eli (Eng Manager): Got it. Second: do we need a manager + director sign-off for >20% comp moves?
Priya (People Ops Partner): yes if comp delta >20% then manager + director + people ops partner approval required. submit using the comp-change form and tag @Priya.
Tori (People Ops): Also remember equity refreshes must be routed separately through Talent and Legal; comp-change form doesn't trigger equity approvals automatically.
Eli (Eng Manager): For leveling, some engineers are asking for a deep dive on criteria. is there a standard rubric?
Noah (People Ops): we have role-level rubrics in the leveling guide in the playbook. managers should surface 2-3 examples of impact aligned to the rubric when submitting.
Priya (People Ops Partner): calibration panels will ask for concrete examples vs adjectives. encourage managers to attach snippets of PR reviews, OKR outcomes, or cross-team project summaries.
Eli (Eng Manager): last one: if a team member is on LOA during the cycle, can they be included?
Tori (People Ops): yes they can be included if they were on the team and manager has evidence pre-LOA. need manager sign-off and People Ops partner ok.
PeopleOpsBot: Reminder scheduled: "Comp-change sign-off deadline" on 2025-06-10 11:00 PT.
Noah (People Ops): Thanks all. I'll publish the short manager FAQ and link it from the handbook.
